title: Ten pieces of the workout tracker have no test at all, including the one that turns a gym's plans into routine folders
what: No test opens ten of this area's files. Among them: the gym plans download, which adds, replaces and relabels routine folders as 'No longer sent' and has its own queue for a sync and a leave-the-gym running at once; the gym measurements and diet plans download; the 'Ask your own AI' read, whose promise is no name, phone or body weight; the badge shelf; the first-routine guide; and saving a photo to the gallery. Two of these files even carry a 'tests only' reset switch that no test ever calls.
expected: Each of these has at least one test that runs it and checks its result, starting with the gym plans download and the AI text read.
fix_line: Add a small test for each untested file, gym plans download and AI text first

title: Old copies of some rules are kept only because tests check them, while the app uses a different copy
what: Several helpers are used by tests and by nothing in the app. The delete-folder question tested here says 'Up next will have no plan until you follow another folder', but the question members really see is written elsewhere and says 'You stop following this plan', so the test passes while the real words go unchecked. The same goes for the 'No routines yet' rule, an older rep-record ladder (the exercise page now uses the records engine's ladder, so there are two rules for the same table), the finish screen's headline line, the rest after the last tick, the month-heading list and a clock helper in the import.
expected: One copy of each rule, the one the app uses, and the tests pointed at that copy; the unused copies removed.
fix_line: Delete the unused copies and move their tests onto the copies the screens really use

title: When the AI-written finish note fails, nothing records why
what: The AI finish note (behind a switch today) throws away every error, from a network drop to a retired model name, and quietly shows the plain note instead. If the AI company retires the model, every member silently loses the AI note and no log line shows it happened.
expected: A failed AI note writes one log line with the reason, so a retired model or a bad key shows up in the logs.
fix_line: Log the error before falling back to the plain note

title: Several reads quietly fall back to a default with no log, so wrong numbers would have no trace
what: Some reads give up without a word. If the exercise page cannot read the member's chosen 'count records from' day, it counts records from all time instead. The finish screen shows no new records if their read fails. The import's pre-check skips its clock repair silently. After a restore, photos that fail to come back from the backup stay missing with no note. A followed plan's start day that fails to save is dropped silently. Each fallback is reasonable, but none leaves a trace.
expected: Each of these fallbacks keeps working as now but writes one log line, so a member's report of wrong records or missing photos can be traced.
fix_line: Add a log line to each of these fallbacks

title: The exercise search speed test can fail on a slow cloud machine
what: One test times the exercise search with a stopwatch and fails if it takes over 3 ms a search or 30 ms to build. It takes the best of several runs, which helps, but a busy or slower cloud machine can still push it over and turn a release check red with no code change.
expected: Speed checks that do not depend on how fast the cloud machine happens to be, or a limit with room for a slow machine plus a retry.
fix_line: Count the work the search does instead of timing it, or widen the limit and allow a retry

title: Two past-workout tests quietly check nothing when run near midnight or a clock change
what: The tests that refuse a past workout ending after now, and one starting later today, read the real clock. Near midnight or in the hour a clock goes back they simply stop early and pass, with no check made and no note that they skipped.
expected: The tests set a fixed clock so they always check the rule, whatever time the cloud machine runs them.
fix_line: Give these tests a fixed clock instead of returning early
